name: Jael
charge: Blessed above women in the tent: the nail, the hammer, and Sisera
summary: Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, because Jabin king of Hazor was at peace with Heber’s house. She covered him with a rug, gave him milk when he asked for water, and when he was sound asleep from exhaustion she took a tent peg and a hammer, crept up to him, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground. The word Deborah had spoken was fulfilled by her hand, that the Lord would hand Sisera over to a woman. The song of Deborah puts the blessing on her: most blessed of the women in tents.
offenseFull: Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, because Jabin king of Hazor was at peace with the house of Heber the Kenite (Judges 4:17-22). Heber, of the descendants of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had separated from the Kenites and pitched his tent near Kedesh (Judges 4:11). Jael went out to meet Sisera, told him to come in and not be afraid, and covered him with a rug; he asked for a little water because he was thirsty, and she opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink and covered him again. He told her to stand in the tent door and, if anyone asked, say no man was there. The captain who had commanded nine hundred chariots of iron was now depending on a woman to hide him.

Then Jael took a tent peg and a hammer, crept up to him as he lay sound asleep from exhaustion, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground, and he died. When Barak came in pursuit, she came out to meet him and showed him the man he was looking for, lying dead with the peg in his temple. The word Deborah had spoken to Barak was fulfilled by her hand: the Lord would hand Sisera over to a woman (Judges 4:9). So God subdued Jabin the king of Canaan that day before Israel (Judges 4:17-23).
judgmentFull: The song of Deborah and Barak pronounces it: Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite is most blessed of women, most blessed of the women in tents. He asked for water and she gave him milk, cream in a bowl fit for nobles; she reached for the peg with one hand and the workman’s hammer with her right, and he collapsed dead at her feet (Judges 5:24-27). Set immediately before that blessing is the curse on Meroz, bitterly cursed by the angel of the Lord because its people did not come to help the Lord against the mighty (Judges 5:23-31). The song puts the two side by side on purpose: a city in Israel that sat out the battle of the Lord and drew a curse, and a woman in a tent who acted and drew a blessing.

It was counted a shame in that day for a man of war to die by a woman’s hand, and the shame followed the next man who earned it. When the millstone crushed Abimelech’s skull at Thebez he quickly called his armourbearer to draw his sword and kill him, so that no one would say a woman had killed him (Judges 9:53-54). Sisera got no such cover. The song then turns to his mother at her window, asking why his chariot is so slow in coming while her wisest ladies answer her with imagined victory and dividing of spoils; she is looking for a son who is never coming home, and Jael has already ended his flight (Judges 5:28-30). The song ends by wishing ruin on the Lord’s enemies and the strength of the rising sun on those who love Him (Judges 5:31).

text.text: Howbeit Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And when he had turned in unto her into the tent, she covered him with a mantle.
And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.
Again he said unto her, Stand in the door of the tent, and it shall be, when any man doth come and enquire of thee, and say, Is there any man here? that thou shalt say, No.

Then Jael Heber’s wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.

And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will shew thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the nail was in his temples.
Now Heber the Kenite, which was of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites, and pitched his tent unto the plain of Zaanaim, which is by Kedesh.

And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the Lord shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Howbeit Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite: for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And when he had turned in unto her into the tent, she covered him with a mantle.
And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.
Again he said unto her, Stand in the door of the tent, and it shall be, when any man doth come and enquire of thee, and say, Is there any man here? that thou shalt say, No.

Then Jael Heber’s wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.

And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will shew thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the nail was in his temples.
So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel.
Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
He asked water, and she gave him milk; she brought forth butter in a lordly dish.
She put her hand to the nail, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer; and with the hammer she smote Sisera, she smote off his head, when she had pierced and stricken through his temples.
At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay down: at her feet he bowed, he fell: where he bowed, there he fell down dead.
Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the Lord, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof; because they came not to the help of the Lord, to the help of the Lord against the mighty.
Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.
He asked water, and she gave him milk; she brought forth butter in a lordly dish.
She put her hand to the nail, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer; and with the hammer she smote Sisera, she smote off his head, when she had pierced and stricken through his temples.
At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay down: at her feet he bowed, he fell: where he bowed, there he fell down dead.
The mother of Sisera looked out at a window, and cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?
Her wise ladies answered her, yea, she returned answer to herself,

Have they not sped? have they not divided the prey; to every man a damsel or two; to Sisera a prey of divers colours, a prey of divers colours of needlework, of divers colours of needlework on both sides, meet for the necks of them that take the spoil?
So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.
And a certain woman cast a piece of a millstone upon Abimelech’s head, and all to brake his skull.

Then he called hastily unto the young man his armourbearer, and said unto him, Draw thy sword, and slay me, that men say not of me, A woman slew him. And his young man thrust him through, and he died.
The mother of Sisera looked out at a window, and cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?
Her wise ladies answered her, yea, she returned answer to herself,

Have they not sped? have they not divided the prey; to every man a damsel or two; to Sisera a prey of divers colours, a prey of divers colours of needlework, of divers colours of needlework on both sides, meet for the necks of them that take the spoil?
So let all thine enemies perish, O Lord: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.
